points.name: 〜にすぎない (ni suginai) — no more than / merely / just
points.shortDescription: Downplays or minimizes something by saying it is nothing more than what it is.
points.formation: Verb (plain form) / Noun / Adjective + にすぎない / にすぎません
points.explanation:
にすぎない is the grammar of the ceiling — it says: this thing does not exceed the modest level being described. The name itself gives it away: 過ぎる means 'to exceed,' and にすぎない is its negative: 'does not go beyond X.' これは私の意見にすぎません — 'This is nothing more than my opinion' — capped at 'one person's view,' nothing more authoritative.

It comes in two flavors: humble (the speaker modestly downplaying their own achievement or status) and dismissive (limiting someone else's claim). 彼の成功は偶然にすぎない — 'His success is nothing but luck' — that reads as a dismissal. In academic and analytical writing, にすぎない is invaluable for scoping a claim honestly: これは一つの仮説にすぎない ('This is merely one hypothesis'). Compare with だけ (only — neutral): にすぎない adds the stronger weight of 'and that's all it amounts to, no more, don't read anything further into it.'
rules: Noun / Plain form + にすぎない = nothing more than / merely / just (downplays significance)
Sets a ceiling — the subject doesn't exceed the modest level described
Comes in two tones: humble self-downplaying, or dismissive limiting of a claim
Compare: だけ (only — neutral); にすぎない (only — stronger dismissive or humble weight)
Negative emphasis: it IS that thing, but it's ONLY that — no more

examples.japanese: これはあくまでも一[ひと]つの仮説[かせつ]にすぎません。
examples.romaji: Kore wa akumade mo hitotsu no kasetsu ni sugimasen.
examples.english: This is merely one hypothesis and nothing more.

examples.japanese: 私[わたし]は日本語学[にほんごがく]習[しゅう]者[もの]にすぎないので、間違[まちが]いがあるかもしれません。
examples.romaji: Watashi wa nihongo gakushuusha ni suginai node, machigai ga aru kamo shiremasen.
examples.english: I am merely a Japanese language learner, so there may be mistakes.

examples.japanese: これは表面上[ひょうめんじょう]の変化[へんか]にすぎず、本質的[ほんしつてき]な問題[もんだい]は解決[かいけつ]されていません。
examples.romaji: Kore wa hyoumen jou no henka ni sugizu, honshitsuteki na mondai wa kaiketsusarete imasen.
examples.english: This is no more than a surface-level change; the fundamental problem has not been resolved.

examples.japanese: 彼[か]の成功[せいこう]は偶然[ぐうぜん]にすぎないと批評家[ひひょうか]は言[い]いますが、私[わたし]はそう思[おも]いません。
examples.romaji: Kare no seikou wa guuzen ni suginai to hihyouka wa iimasu ga, watashi wa sou omoimasen.
examples.english: Critics say his success is nothing but luck, but I don't think so.

points.flashcardAnswer: Downplays or minimizes something by saying it is nothing more than what it is.

practice.prompt: What does 〜にすぎない mean?
choices: at least / more than
(nothing) more than / merely / only — downplays the significance of X, implying it's less impressive than it seems
because of
as a result of
practice.explanation: 〜にすぎない = nothing more than / merely. これは偶然[ぐうぜん]にすぎない = this is nothing more than coincidence. It downplays or minimizes the importance of something. Often implies 'don't read too much into it.'

practice.prompt: Which correctly says 'This is merely a rumor'?
choices: これは噂[うわさ]にすぎない。
これは噂[うわさ]ばかりだ。
これは噂[うわさ]というものだ。
これは噂[うわさ]だけだ。
practice.explanation: Noun + にすぎない: 噂[うわさ] + にすぎない = nothing more than a rumor. にすぎない downplays the noun — the implication is 'don't take it as more than a rumor.'

practice.prompt: Which means 'He is just a beginner'?
choices: 彼[かれ]は初心者[しょしんしゃ]にすぎない。
彼[かれ]は初心者[しょしんしゃ]だけだ。
彼[かれ]は初心者[しょしんしゃ]というものだ。
彼[かれ]は初心者[しょしんしゃ]ばかりだ。
practice.explanation: Noun + にすぎない: 初心者[しょしんしゃ] + にすぎない = nothing more than a beginner. Downplays his level — implying 'he's not much, just a beginner.'

practice.prompt: Which correctly says 'What I said was merely a joke'?
choices: 私[わたし]が言[い]ったのは冗談[じょうだん]にすぎなかった。
私[わたし]が言[い]ったのは冗談[じょうだん]だけだった。
私[わたし]が言[い]ったのは冗談[じょうだん]というものだった。
私[わたし]が言[い]ったのは冗談[じょうだん]のはずだった。
practice.explanation: Noun + にすぎなかった (past): 冗談[じょうだん] + にすぎなかった = was nothing more than a joke. Downplays the severity of what was said.

practice.prompt: What FORMATION does にすぎない use?
choices: Verb te-form + にすぎない
Noun / Verb plain form / い-adj plain / な-adj stem + にすぎない
Verb masu-stem + にすぎない
Only noun + にすぎない
practice.explanation: にすぎない attaches to: Noun (噂[うわさ]にすぎない), Verb plain (言[い]っているにすぎない), い-adj plain (高[たか]いにすぎない), な-adj stem (便利[べんり]なにすぎない). It downplays whatever precedes it.

practice.prompt: Which correctly says 'This number is just a rough estimate'?
choices: この数字[すうじ]はあくまで概算[がいさん]にすぎない。
この数字[すうじ]はあくまで概算[がいさん]だけだ。
この数字[すうじ]はあくまで概算[がいさん]というものだ。
この数字[すうじ]はあくまで概算[がいさん]のはずだ。
practice.explanation: Noun + にすぎない: 概算[がいさん] + にすぎない = nothing more than a rough estimate. あくまで reinforces the downplaying sense: 'this is purely/merely an estimate.'

practice.prompt: Which means 'She merely answered the question asked'?
choices: 彼女[かのじょ]は聞[き]かれたことに答[こた]えたにすぎない。
彼女[かのじょ]は聞[き]かれたことに答[こた]えたばかりだ。
彼女[かのじょ]は聞[き]かれたことに答[こた]えただけだ。
彼女[かのじょ]は聞[き]かれたことに答[こた]えたはずだ。
practice.explanation: Verb plain past + にすぎない: 答[こた]えた + にすぎない = nothing more than answered. Downplays the action — she only did what was asked, nothing more.

practice.prompt: Which correctly says 'This is just one example'?
choices: これは一例[いちれい]にすぎない。
これは一例[いちれい]だけだ。
これは一例[いちれい]というものだ。
これは一例[いちれい]ほどだ。
practice.explanation: Noun + にすぎない: 一例[いちれい] + にすぎない = nothing more than one example. Downplays the scope — 'this is just a single example, don't generalize from it.'

practice.prompt: What nuance does にすぎない often carry?
choices: It expresses admiration
It implies the thing is less than it appears or less than one might expect — a downgrading/minimizing nuance
It expresses regret
It expresses contrast
practice.explanation: にすぎない = minimization/downgrading. Often used to: (1) correct overestimation ('it's just X, don't overrate it'); (2) be modest about oneself; (3) indicate that something has no further significance beyond what it literally is.

practice.prompt: Which correctly says 'I'm only an ordinary office worker'?
choices: 私[わたし]はただのサラリーマンにすぎない。
私[わたし]はただのサラリーマンだけだ。
私[わたし]はただのサラリーマンというものだ。
私[わたし]はただのサラリーマンのはずだ。
practice.explanation: Noun + にすぎない: サラリーマン + にすぎない = nothing more than an ordinary office worker. ただの reinforces the modesty/minimization.

practice.prompt: Which means 'This technology is just a prototype'?
choices: この技術[ぎじゅつ]はプロトタイプにすぎない。
この技術[ぎじゅつ]はプロトタイプだけだ。
この技術[ぎじゅつ]はプロトタイプというものだ。
この技術[ぎじゅつ]はプロトタイプのはずだ。
practice.explanation: Noun + にすぎない: プロトタイプ + にすぎない = nothing more than a prototype. Downplays the technology — it's not a finished product.

practice.prompt: Which correctly says 'The proposal is merely a starting point for discussion'?
choices: この提案[ていあん]は議論[ぎろん]のスタートポイントにすぎない。
この提案[ていあん]は議論[ぎろん]のスタートポイントだけだ。
この提案[ていあん]は議論[ぎろん]のスタートポイントというものだ。
この提案[ていあん]は議論[ぎろん]のスタートポイントのはずだ。
practice.explanation: Noun + にすぎない: スタートポイント + にすぎない = nothing more than a starting point. Downplays the proposal — it's only the beginning of discussion, not a finished plan.

practice.prompt: How does にすぎない compare to だけ (only)?
choices: They are identical
にすぎない is more emphatic in downplaying — it implies 'don't even consider it more than X'; だけ is a neutral limiter that just states the quantity/scope without a minimizing nuance
だけ is more emphatic
にすぎない is only for verbs
practice.explanation: にすぎない = minimizing emphasis ('this is MERELY X, don't overestimate'). だけ = neutral limiter ('only X, no more'). 一例[いちれい]にすぎない = it's merely an example (downplaying, cautionary). 一例[いちれい]だけだ = there's only one example (factual count).

practice.prompt: Which correctly says 'My Japanese is still at the level where I can only have daily conversations'?
choices: 私[わたし]の日本語[にほんご]は日常会話[にちじょうかいわ]ができる程度[ていど]にすぎない。
私[わたし]の日本語[にほんご]は日常会話[にちじょうかいわ]ができる程度[ていど]だけだ。
私[わたし]の日本語[にほんご]は日常会話[にちじょうかいわ]ができる程度[ていど]というものだ。
私[わたし]の日本語[にほんご]は日常会話[にちじょうかいわ]ができる程度[ていど]のはずだ。
practice.explanation: Noun/degree + にすぎない: 程度[ていど] + にすぎない = nothing more than that level. Modest self-evaluation: my Japanese is only at daily conversation level, no more.

practice.prompt: Which means 'He is just saying what he thinks — he has no ill intent'?
choices: 彼[かれ]は思[おも]ったことを言[い]っているにすぎない — 悪意[あくい]はない。
彼[かれ]は思[おも]ったことを言[い]っているだけだ — 悪意[あくい]はない。
彼[かれ]は思[おも]ったことを言[い]っているというものだ — 悪意[あくい]はない。
彼[かれ]は思[おも]ったことを言[い]っているはずだ — 悪意[あくい]はない。
practice.explanation: Verb plain + にすぎない: 言[い]っている + にすぎない = nothing more than saying what he thinks. Minimizes the action to defend him: 'he's merely speaking his mind.'

practice.prompt: Which correctly says 'This is just a temporary solution'?
choices: これは一時的[いちじてき]な対応[たいおう]にすぎない。
これは一時的[いちじてき]な対応[たいおう]だけだ。
これは一時的[いちじてき]な対応[たいおう]というものだ。
これは一時的[いちじてき]な対応[たいおう]のはずだ。
practice.explanation: Noun + にすぎない: 一時的[いちじてき]な対応[たいおう] + にすぎない = nothing more than a temporary solution. Downplays the measure — implies it's not a real fix.

practice.prompt: Which sentence BEST illustrates にすぎない correcting an overestimation?
choices: 彼[かれ]は天才[てんさい]にすぎない。(says he's merely a genius — downplays? — awkward)
それは偶然[ぐうぜん]の一致[いっち]にすぎない。(it's merely a coincidence — corrects overreading of a coincidence as meaningful)
彼女[かのじょ]は学生[がくせい]にすぎない。(she's merely a student — contextual)
これは問題[もんだい]にすぎない。(this is merely a problem — weak)
practice.explanation: それは偶然[ぐうぜん]の一致[いっち]にすぎない = it's nothing more than a coincidence. Classic use: someone may be seeing a meaningful pattern, but にすぎない corrects the interpretation ('you're reading too much into it — it's just coincidence').

practice.prompt: Which correctly says 'The discount is merely 5% — it's not much of a deal'?
choices: 割引[わりびき]はたった5%にすぎない — 大[たい]したことはない。
割引[わりびき]はたった5%だけだ — 大[たい]したことはない。
割引[わりびき]はたった5%というものだ — 大[たい]したことはない。
割引[わりびき]はたった5%のはずだ — 大[たい]したことはない。
practice.explanation: Noun/number + にすぎない: 5% + にすぎない = nothing more than 5%. たった reinforces the minimizing sense. The discount is being downplayed as insignificant.

practice.prompt: Which means 'What you call wisdom is merely accumulated experience'?
choices: あなたが知恵[ちえ]と呼[よ]ぶものは、積[つ]み重[かさ]ねた経験[けいけん]にすぎない。
あなたが知恵[ちえ]と呼[よ]ぶものは、積[つ]み重[かさ]ねた経験[けいけん]だけだ。
あなたが知恵[ちえ]と呼[よ]ぶものは、積[つ]み重[かさ]ねた経験[けいけん]というものだ。
あなたが知恵[ちえ]と呼[よ]ぶものは、積[つ]み重[かさ]ねた経験[けいけん]のはずだ。
practice.explanation: Noun + にすぎない: 経験[けいけん] + にすぎない = nothing more than experience. Deflates the grand concept of 'wisdom' to something more mundane — just accumulated experience.

practice.prompt: Which correctly says 'I merely stated the facts — I didn't exaggerate'?
choices: 私[わたし]は事実[じじつ]を述[の]べたにすぎない — 誇張[こちょう]はしていない。
私[わたし]は事実[じじつ]を述[の]べただけだ — 誇張[こちょう]はしていない。
私[わたし]は事実[じじつ]を述[の]べたというものだ — 誇張[こちょう]はしていない。
私[わたし]は事実[じじつ]を述[の]べたはずだ — 誇張[こちょう]はしていない。
practice.explanation: Verb past + にすぎない: 述[の]べた + にすぎない = nothing more than stated. Defends the action as minimal and pure: 'I only stated facts.'

points.name: 〜に限[かぎ]らず (ni kagirazu) — not limited to / not just / beyond
points.shortDescription: Extends scope beyond a specific entity: 'not only X, but beyond X as well'.
points.formation: Noun + に限らず + broader scope or additional examples
points.explanation:
に限らず comes from 限る (to limit) flipped to negative: 'not limited to.' It expands scope beyond the noun it attaches to. 日本人に限らず、外国人もこの祭りを楽しめます: 'Not limited to Japanese people, foreigners can also enjoy this festival' — you start with the expected or obvious group and then open the door wider.

This scope-expanding function makes に限らず more formal than だけでなく (not only...but also), and it's the preferred choice in written announcements, reports, and formal speeches where you want to make a broad, inclusive statement.

Two related forms are worth knowing: に限っては (only / limited to) does the opposite — it restricts to a specific case, often with an ironic 'the one exception is...' flavor. に限り (formal: limited to only) appears in notices and official announcements. The pattern to remember: expanding scope → に限らず; restricting to one case → に限っては.
rules: Noun + に限らず = not limited to [noun] / not just [noun] (broadening scope)
Sets up a specific group then extends the point to a wider group
More formal than だけでなく (not only); preferred in writing, formal speech
Related: に限って = only / in the case of only [noun] (restricting, often ironic)
Related: に限り = limited to only [noun] (formal restriction, used in notices)

examples.japanese: この問題[もんだい]は日本[にっぽん]に限[かぎ]らず、世界中[せかいじゅう]で起[お]きています。
examples.romaji: Kono mondai wa Nihon ni kagirazu, sekaijuu de okite imasu.
examples.english: This problem is not limited to Japan — it is happening all over the world.

examples.japanese: スポーツに限[かぎ]らず、音楽[おんがく]や芸術[げいじゅつ]でも努力[どりょく]は大切[たいせつ]です。
examples.romaji: Supootsu ni kagirazu, ongaku ya geijutsu demo doryoku wa taisetsu desu.
examples.english: Not limited to sports — in music and art too, effort is important.

examples.japanese: 若者[わかもの]に限[かぎ]らず、中高年[ちゅうこうねん]の方々[かたがた]もスマートフォンを使[つか]っています。
examples.romaji: Wakamono ni kagirazu, chuukouen no katagata mo sumaatofon wo tsukatte imasu.
examples.english: Not limited to young people — middle-aged and older people also use smartphones.

examples.japanese: 専門家[せんもんか]に限[かぎ]らず、一般[いっぱん]の市民[しみん]も政策[せいさく]についての意見[いけん]を持[も]つべきです。
examples.romaji: Senmonka ni kagirazu, ippan no shimin mo seisaku ni tsuite no iken wo motsu beki desu.
examples.english: Not limited to experts — ordinary citizens too should have opinions on policy.

points.flashcardAnswer: Extends scope beyond a specific entity: 'not only X, but beyond X as well'.

practice.prompt: What does 〜に限[かぎ]らず mean?
choices: limited to / restricted to X
not only X / not limited to X — extends scope beyond X to include other things too
as many as X
no more than X
practice.explanation: 〜に限[かぎ]らず = not only X / not limited to X. 子[こ]どもに限[かぎ]らず大人[おとな]も楽[たの]しめる = not only children but adults can enjoy it too. に限[かぎ]る (to be limited to) → に限[かぎ]らず (not limited to) = scope extension.

practice.prompt: Which correctly says 'Not only in Japan but in other countries too, sushi is popular'?
choices: 日本[にっぽん]に限[かぎ]らず他[ほか]の国[くに]でも、寿司[すし]は人気[にんき]だ。
日本[にっぽん]だけでなく他[ほか]の国[くに]でも、寿司[すし]は人気[にんき]だ。
日本[にっぽん]に限[かぎ]って他[ほか]の国[くに]でも、寿司[すし]は人気[にんき]だ。
日本[にっぽん]のみならず他[ほか]の国[くに]でも、寿司[すし]は人気[にんき]だ。
practice.explanation: Noun + に限[かぎ]らず: 日本[にっぽん] + に限[かぎ]らず = not limited to Japan. 他[ほか]の国[くに]でも = in other countries too. Extends the scope beyond Japan.

practice.prompt: Which means 'Not only students but also teachers should read this book'?
choices: 学生[がくせい]に限[かぎ]らず先生[せんせい]もこの本[ほん]を読[よ]むべきだ。
学生[がくせい]だけでなく先生[せんせい]もこの本[ほん]を読[よ]むべきだ。
学生[がくせい]に限[かぎ]って先生[せんせい]もこの本[ほん]を読[よ]むべきだ。
学生[がくせい]のみならず先生[せんせい]もこの本[ほん]を読[よ]むべきだ。
practice.explanation: Noun + に限[かぎ]らず: 学生[がくせい] + に限[かぎ]らず = not limited to students. 先生[せんせい]も = teachers too. に限[かぎ]らず extends the recommendation beyond students.

practice.prompt: Which correctly says 'Not only on weekdays but also on weekends the store is open'?
choices: 平日[へいじつ]に限[かぎ]らず週末[しゅうまつ]も店[みせ]は開[ひら]いている。
平日[へいじつ]だけでなく週末[しゅうまつ]も店[みせ]は開[ひら]いている。
平日[へいじつ]に限[かぎ]って週末[しゅうまつ]も店[みせ]は開[ひら]いている。
平日[へいじつ]のみならず週末[しゅうまつ]も店[みせ]は開[ひら]いている。
practice.explanation: Noun + に限[かぎ]らず: 平日[へいじつ] + に限[かぎ]らず = not limited to weekdays. 週末[しゅうまつ]も = on weekends too. に限[かぎ]らず extends the scope of operating days.

practice.prompt: に限[かぎ]らず vs. だけでなく — which is more FORMAL?
choices: They are identical in formality
に限[かぎ]らず is more formal/written; だけでなく is more casual/conversational
だけでなく is more formal
に限[かぎ]らず is only for spoken Japanese
practice.explanation: に限[かぎ]らず is more formal and literary. だけでなく is more conversational. Both mean 'not only X.' In formal essays, reports, or official statements, に限[かぎ]らず is preferred. In casual speech, だけでなく is more natural.

practice.prompt: Which correctly says 'Not only English but also French is spoken in that country'?
choices: 英語[えいご]に限[かぎ]らずフランス語[ご]もその国[くに]では話[はな]されている。
英語[えいご]だけでなくフランス語[ご]もその国[くに]では話[はな]されている。
英語[えいご]に限[かぎ]ってフランス語[ご]もその国[くに]では話[はな]されている。
英語[えいご]のみならずフランス語[ご]もその国[くに]では話[はな]されている。

practice.prompt: Which means 'Not only price but also quality is important when buying something'?
choices: 価格[かかく]に限[かぎ]らず品質[ひんしつ]も、物[もの]を買[か]うときに重要[じゅうよう]だ。

practice.prompt: Which correctly says 'Not only experts but also beginners can use this software'?
choices: 専門家[せんもんか]に限[かぎ]らず初心者[しょしんしゃ]もこのソフトを使[つか]える。
専門家[せんもんか]だけでなく初心者[しょしんしゃ]もこのソフトを使[つか]える。
専門家[せんもんか]に限[かぎ]って初心者[しょしんしゃ]もこのソフトを使[つか]える。
専門家[せんもんか]のみならず初心者[しょしんしゃ]もこのソフトを使[つか]える。
practice.explanation: Noun + に限[かぎ]らず: 専門家[せんもんか] + に限[かぎ]らず = not limited to experts. 初心者[しょしんしゃ]も = beginners too. Extends the user scope beyond experts.

practice.prompt: に限[かぎ]らず comes from に限[かぎ]る (limited to). Which BEST explains this relationship?
choices: There is no relationship
に限[かぎ]る = X only (restricted scope); に限[かぎ]らず = not X only (negated restriction = scope extension). に限[かぎ]らず literally = 'without being limited to'
に限[かぎ]らず is the polite form of に限[かぎ]る

points.name: 〜はもとより (wa moto yori) — to say nothing of / not only...but also
points.shortDescription: Establishes that even the expected/easier case is true, and the harder case follows as well.
points.formation: Noun A + はもとより + Noun B / clause + も
points.explanation:
はもとより is a formal, literary pattern meaning 'to say nothing of' or 'not only X, but even Y.' It has a two-tier structure: the element before はもとより is the expected, obvious case — the baseline that 'goes without saying' — while the element after is the more impressive or noteworthy addition. 英語はもとより、フランス語も話せます: 'Not only English (the expected baseline), she can also speak French' — the English fluency is unremarkable; the French is where things get impressive. This direction matters: the more surprising or notable element always comes after はもとより.

Note on register: はもとより is distinctly formal and literary. It has a similar-meaning everyday counterpart, はもちろん ('of course / naturally, and also X'), which fits comfortably in general writing and conversation. はもとより belongs in written formal contexts, business writing, and polished speeches where the higher register is appropriate.
rules: Noun A + はもとより + B + も = not only A (expected) but even B (impressive addition)
A is the baseline expected element ('goes without saying'); B is the more noteworthy one
More formal/literary than はもちろん (everyday) and だけでなく (not only)
The element before はもとより is the given; the addition after is what's noteworthy
Often structured: 〜はもとより、〜も + positive quality/action

practice.prompt: What does 〜はもとより mean?
choices: although / even though
not only X — takes X as a given and goes further to include Y; even more than X; needless to say X
from the beginning / originally
limited to X
practice.explanation: 〜はもとより = not only X (but Y too) / needless to say X / X goes without saying. 日本語[にほんご]はもとより英語[えいご]も話[はな]せる = needless to say Japanese, (she) can also speak English. X (more obvious) is taken for granted; Y (less obvious) is added.

practice.explanation: Noun + はもとより: 日本語[にほんご] + はもとより = needless to say Japanese. フランス語[ご]も = French too. The Japanese ability is taken as a given; French is the impressive addition.
